clue.text: Bottom team after defender

indicators.note: after places the team word behind the defender word

parts.note: a back is a defending player in football or hockey
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A struggling bottom-of-the-table club whose problems lie behind the defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Your posterior or rear end is the part you sit on, a synonym.

clue.text: Casually raise the volume?

parts.note: sounds like turning up the sound, but means picking up a book and leafing through it idly

explanation.surface: A suggestion to nonchalantly turn up the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' means loudness in the surface but a book in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To leaf idly through a book or shop without firm intent.

clue.text: It comes from Mecca, this instruction book

indicators.note: comes from means the answer's letters are produced by reworking the following words

explanation.surface: A claim that a religious manual originates in the holy city of Islam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes from' rearranges MECCA THIS; Mecca suggests Islam, but the answer is a Christian question-and-answer manual.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual of religious teaching set out as questions and answers.

clue.text: Water ice, a bit of a refresher between times

indicators.note: a bit of means the answer lies within the run of letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A water ice served as a little refreshment between courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' takes the run inside refreSHER BETween; 'times' completes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet, a frozen dessert made from fruit juice.

clue.text: Draw cheque

definitions.meaning: to draw up, as a plan or document
a banker's order to pay, issued by a bank

explanation.surface: An instruction to write out a cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: Both to sketch out a first version of a document and a bank order for payment.

clue.text: Cat's-cradle land?

parts.note: read not as the string game but as the cradle, or birthplace, of a breed of cat: the long-haired breed named after its homeland

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about the country where the children's string game began.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat's cradle is a string game played between two pairs of hands; here it means the land where a cat breed was born. The Persian cat takes its name from the old name for Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: The Persian cat breed is named after the old country name for Iran, its supposed homeland.

clue.text: Variable pitch up in Morecambe

indicators.note: in means the turned word goes inside the comedian's first name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was half of the British comedy duo Morecambe and Wise

indicators.note: up means the word for pitch reads upwards in this down entry

parts.note: pitch is tar

explanation.surface: Unsettled weather or a bumpy football pitch in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TAR into RAT. Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort but stands for the comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconsistent or unpredictable, a synonym.

clue.text: Surreptitious attempt announced in Irish town

indicators.note: announced means the words are spoken and heard as another spelling

parts.note: a sly go is a sneaky try

explanation.surface: A secret try made public in a town in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A town and county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Like some wells with a set rainfall

indicators.note: fall, the second half of rainfall, means the preceding letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Certain wells are fed by steady rainfall.
explanation.walkthrough: The clever trick is that 'rainfall' splits: RAIN is fodder and 'fall' is the signal to scramble A SET RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An artesian well taps water under pressure that rises without pumping.

clue.text: In matters spiritual, he is coasting freely

definitions.text: In matters spiritual, he is coasting freely

indicators.note: freely means the letters of the word coasting move about at will into a new order

explanation.surface: A man drifting along without commitment in matters of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges COASTING, and the whole clue describes such a person: one who drifts with no fixed belief about God.
explanation.definitionFit: One who holds that God's existence cannot be known commits to no faith.

clue.text: In a bad way, get NHS trial done

definitions.text: In a bad way, get NHS trial done

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are put in a bad way, that is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient in poor health urges that a National Health Service trial be completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a bad way' scrambles GET NHS TRIAL DONE (NHS is Britain's National Health Service), and the whole clue doubles as the definition: a gravely ill patient might want such a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital phrase for a patient in critical condition whose life is at risk.

clue.text: Fire bar an old piece of brass

parts.note: to fire someone from a job is to sack them
bar, meaning except, is but

explanation.surface: An instruction to dismiss a band's old brass instrument, or a barred fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' here is the brass section of a band, not money or metal. A sackbut is the Renaissance ancestor of the trombone.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut was an early trombone, a historic brass instrument.

clue.text: You can't get out if these are not kept open

definitions.text: You can't get out if these are not kept open

parts.words: You can't get out if these are not kept open
parts.note: reads like doors or exits, but means the choices left to you: close them off and you have no way out of a situation

explanation.surface: A safety notice about fire doors that must never be locked.
explanation.definitionFit: Choices or alternatives; keeping them available is how one avoids being trapped by a decision.

clue.text: Suspicion of corrosion after condensation

indicators.note: after places the corrosion word behind the condensation word

parts.note: mist is fine water droplets condensed in the air
rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: A worry that rust will follow once damp has formed on metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrust or doubt about someone's honesty, a synonym.

clue.text: Play without stress?

parts.note: reads as relaxed play, but means acting a part with too little emphasis

explanation.surface: Advice to play a game in a relaxed way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' is acting a role and 'stress' is emphasis, not anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform a role with too much restraint, giving it too little emphasis.

clue.text: Butterfly — one of a pair often seen upside down

definitions.meaning: a common European butterfly with a white ...-shaped mark beneath its wing

definitions.text: one of a pair often seen upside down
definitions.meaning: the opening inverted ... of a quotation is the punctuation mark turned upside down

explanation.surface: A butterfly that, like many insects, hangs upside down in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a butterfly species named for its white mark and the punctuation mark that, inverted, opens a quotation.

clue.text: Villain's violent crimes against a worker

indicators.note: against means the insect is set up next to the scrambled letters
violent means the letters of crimes are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A wicked man's brutal offences against an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' rearranges CRIMES into MISCRE; 'against' puts ANT beside it. The definition's 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or scoundrel, a synonym.

clue.text: Thick woods always used for bow-mast support

parts.note: a forest is dense woodland
ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Dense timber always being chosen to support a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: A forestay is the rope or wire running from the foremast to the bow of a sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay running forward from the foremast to the bow, holding the mast up.

clue.text: See 'ere, I say, window does not open!

indicators.note: does not open means the word for the window loses its opening letter

parts.note: a dormer is a window set in a sloping roof

explanation.surface: A Cockney grumbling to a friend that a window is stuck shut.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'sea ear' said in Cockney ('See 'ere'), 'I say' marking the sound: the sea ear is another name for this Channel Islands shellfish. 'does not open' takes the D off DORMER.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer, or abalone, is a shellfish also called the sea ear for its ear-like shell.

clue.text: Redskin's whip?

parts.note: a dated term for a Native American suggests a weapon, but read as red, uncooked skin made into a lash

explanation.surface: A question about a Native American's lash, in an old Western.
explanation.walkthrough: The dated word 'Redskin' splits as RED (raw, uncured) and SKIN (hide).
explanation.definitionFit: A whip of untanned leather, as used by cowboys.

clue.text: Potatoes in this style expected to include game?

indicators.note: to include means the word for expected wraps round the game

parts.note: something expected is due
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: Guessing that a dish of potatoes should come with game meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like meat to go with potatoes; it is chess. Duchesse potatoes are mashed with egg and piped into rosettes before baking.
explanation.definitionFit: A French culinary term for mashed potato piped and baked, named after a duchess.

clue.text: One who helps another to a seat

definitions.text: One who helps another to a seat

parts.words: One who helps another to a seat
parts.note: sounds like an usher at a theatre, but means a voter putting a candidate into a parliamentary seat

explanation.surface: An usher showing a guest to a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' is a seat in Parliament, not a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter chooses a representative and so helps them into office.

clue.text: Obsessed by this classic sort of novel?

parts.note: got, as in he has really got it bad, means obsessed
hic is the Latin, or classic language, word for this

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on a particular kind of classic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classic' points to Latin, where hic means 'this'. Gothic novels are tales of horror and gloomy castles.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre of fiction with horror, mystery and gloomy settings.

clue.text: Place in Regent's Park, perhaps, for Oscar Wilde in ""The Sea Goose'"?

indicators.note: in means the playwright's initials go inside the bird's name

parts.note: the ember goose is an old name for the great northern diver, a sea bird
O and W are the initials of the Irish playwright

explanation.surface: Imagining the playwright Oscar Wilde starring in a play called The Sea Goose staged in a London park.
explanation.walkthrough: Regent's Park is a London royal park full of shady arbours. The quotation looks like a play title; it is the bird, the ember goose.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something within a leafy arbour, like those in a large garden or park.

clue.text: People look down on such house-calling

definitions.text: People look down on such house-calling

parts.words: People look down on such house-calling
parts.note: sounds like snobbish disdain for door-to-door visits, but players keep their eyes down on their cards, and calling house means a win

explanation.surface: Snobs sneering at salesmen who call door to door.
explanation.walkthrough: In this British numbers game, 'eyes down' starts play and a winner shouts 'House!'
explanation.definitionFit: The numbers game where players mark cards as numbers are called, a win claimed by shouting house.

clue.text: Brighten No 10 for so long

parts.note: to brighten someone is to cheer them
the number ten written as the figures one and zero, which look like I and O

explanation.surface: Cheering up the Prime Minister's residence for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 looks like Downing Street, the British Prime Minister's home; it is just the digits 1 and 0 read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual British farewell, like goodbye.

clue.text: Climber's first over the mound, the blockhead

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the letter above the mound
first means just the opening letter of the word Climber's

parts.note: a hump is a mound

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is the first to cross a hill, the idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or dolt, a synonym.

clue.text: Was it sworn at Versailles in a tie-break situation?

definitions.text: Was it sworn at Versailles in a tie-break situation?

parts.words: Was it sworn at Versailles in a tie-break situation?
parts.note: the tie-break suggests a tennis match; the pledge sworn at Versailles in 1789 by the Third Estate was made in a real tennis hall

explanation.surface: A joke question about a tennis player swearing during a tie-break at a French palace.
explanation.walkthrough: In June 1789 the French Third Estate, locked out of their hall at Versailles, met in a nearby real tennis court and swore not to disband until France had a constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic pledge of the National Assembly at the start of the French Revolution, named after its venue.

clue.text: The old sign of those not quite gentlemen

parts.note: ye is an old form of the word the
an omen is a sign

explanation.surface: An old sign marking social inferiors who fall just short of the gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeomen were farmers owning their own land, ranked just below the gentry in English society.
explanation.definitionFit: Small landowning farmers formed the class just below the gentry in old England.

clue.text: Notedly theatrical Scotch governor embraces English artist

indicators.note: embraces means the measuring device wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: an optic is the measuring device on an upturned spirits bottle in a pub, controlling each pour of whisky
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A theatrical Scottish governor hugging an English painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch governor' looks like a Scottish ruler; it is the pub optic that regulates measures of Scotch whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera-like, melodramatic and given to music, so theatrical in a musical way.
